To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the elastic modulus of lipid membranes is not constant but rather depends upon the lipid composition and temperature, the critical tension of membranes is not constant and can vary with lipid composition and temperature and that the material properties of two phase lipid membranes are not the same as those of single phase lipid membranes.

(1) the elasticity of POPC/DPPPC vesicles is independent of DPPPC fraction, (2) the elasticity decreases with temperature in a manner consistent with a decrease in interfacial energy, (3) the critical tension decreases with temperature, and (4) the critical tension of two-phase membranes is lower than that of pure Lα membranes.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical properties of lipid vesicle membranes.
the mechanical properties of lipid bilayer membranes and their dependence on the state of the membrane and the presence of membrane inhomogeneities.
the mechanical properties of lipid vesicle in the liquid crystalline and coexistence regimes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the material properties of Lα and two-phase vesicles differ in ways that can be explained by the different structures and compositions of these membranes.

the elastic properties of lipid vesicle membranes are dependent on the phase state and composition of the membrane, but the elastic properties of membranes with gel phase domains are dependent on the gel network morphology and not the bulk elastic properties of the gel phase.
the elastic modulus and critical tension of Lα vesicle are temperature dependent, but are independent of DPC concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the material properties of Lα membranes are relatively insensitive to the presence of gel domains, but are strongly dependent upon temperature.
lipid vesicles in the two-phase coexistence regime are more elastic and weaker than Lα vesicles.
the mechanical properties of lipid membranes can be altered by changing the phase state, the presence of phase coexistence, and the composition of the membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the material properties of membranes are not only dependent upon lipid composition, but also on the phase state of the lipids.
lipid vesicles with coexisting phases have distinct mechanical properties from those in the Lα phase.
the mechanical properties of lipid vesicle membranes are highly sensitive to their thermodynamic state.
